tasks.title: Cell registry 1/5: registry module, management CLI, single grid module
tasks.notes: Part of the cell-registry epic (tickets 29-33, one new branch off main, one PR; do NOT use the bakeoff-r004 branch). DESIGN (agreed in grilling session): world data lives in the active world: registry/cells.json + registry/features.json, sparse (absent cell = empty), written ONLY through one registry module (atomic write, sorted keys); LLM reads only via a documented management command. Cell record: ground none|ghost|ghost+features|generated; trees bool; decor bool; marker up|none; hold reason|null. Derived, never stored: empty, DONE, current cell (= marker cell), a cell's features. DONE = ground generated + trees + decor + every registered feature in the cell built + no marker + no open OSM-coverage warnings. Feature record: id = build slug (matches site/builds/<name>.json), name, cells touched, status planned|in-progress|built (one status per feature). Invariants enforced in code (refused write raises error naming the rule, nothing changes): single marker; ghost+features only on ghost ground; trees/decor only on generated ground; rebuilding ground clears trees+decor; reopening a feature clears trees+decor in every cell it touches. Management CLI with clear docs: query (is feature X built, what is left in cell C, status), register feature (explicit list; helper proposes OSM candidates), hold set/clear, dismiss OSM warning with reason. GRID: one cellmath module owns cell size, bounds, cell->region mapping, ring order, parse_cell and the id format; delete the other definitions (world_frame.CELL/cell_of/cell_bounds/parse_cell, coverage.cell_of/cell_bbox, pass_mask.CELL_SIZE, site_stages.CELL_SHIFT, ground_sources.mc_tile_for_cell, ref_manifest.mc_tile_id, lidar_ghost use of CELL_SHIFT). Cell id is always the string 'tx,tz' (e.g. 48,-44); 'm44' spelling only inside file names. Origin cell and cell size move into the world's world-frame.json (remove hard-coded ORIGIN_CELL in cellmath.py and CENTRE in site_status.py). Tests for all invariants. Done 2026-10-21 on cell-registry-tickets: scripts/cell_registry.py + CLI; cellmath owns grid (size/origin from world-frame cell); invariant tests; callers delegate. World checkout: config/world-frame.json cell block + empty registry/.

tasks.title: Cell registry 2/5: make build commands update the registry automatically
tasks.notes: PRINCIPLE: the registry is updated by code as a side effect of build commands, not by LLM-followed rules. ground_layer/trees_layer/decor_layer set ground/trees/decor on a clean readback only. site_kit.apply: feature status in-progress on begin, built only on clean readback (zero mismatches; mismatches stay in-progress); cells touched overwritten from the real footprint. cell_marker raise/clear sets marker (marker no longer counts as work or as a STAGES entry). lidar_ghost keeps its state machine but writes only to the registry: ghost lay-down around the marker cell (default ring 2; ground none->ghost / ghost+features); real feature apply strips ghost features first (ghost+features -> ghost); real ground apply -> generated and drops ghost features; markers never count as real work. Every block-removing command clears the matching flags in the same step: mask_undo, strip_cell_above_ground, ghost supersede/strip, site_recover. A failed apply never sets flags. Feature specs stay in site/builds/<name>.json; *-cells.json ownership files stay as block-level evidence the registry points to (not a second status record). Per-run detail (readback, snapshot, structure/from/to) goes to the existing *-result.json / *-backup.json; masks stay under verification/site/masks. Tests per writer. Done 2026-10-21 on cell-registry-tickets: registry_hooks + site_kit.apply begin/clean, cell_marker raise/clear/adopt, mask_undo, strip_cell_above_ground, site_recover rollback, lidar_ghost feature strip demotion. tasks.title: Cell registry 4/5: repair cell, whole-world backup pair, logout gate, verify
tasks.notes: repair <cell>: back up ONLY the impacted region files (region holding the cell plus any region its features/trees/decor spill into, from *-cells.json footprints and masks) together with that cell's registry record; wipe only that cell's columns to air above bedrock; replay from the registry clipped to the cell bounds (ghost ground/features if ghost state, else ground, features in registry order, trees, decor; features from site/builds specs); re-raise marker if it was up; if any step fails, clear flags for that step and all later ones so next picks it up. 'undo repair' restores the region files and the saved registry record. Bake-off: wipe the WHOLE world each round, restore ONE whole-world backup paired with a whole-registry copy (no per-cell slices); update model_bakeoff.restore_ghost_step and region_backup. Raw region_backup restore of a partial snapshot is refused (error points at the proper undo/redo command) except via repair-undo and the full-world bake-off restore. LOGOUT GATE: every command that rewrites region files (repair, undo repair, bake-off wipe/restore, dryrun_reset) refuses without --confirm-logged-out, stops and plays the need-you sound asking the user to log out; second guard checks session.lock / a running server holding the save and refuses even with the flag. VERIFY (report only, exit non-zero on any error): invariants; marker rings vs registry (exactly the marked cell has a stripe ring); region files exist for cells with ground and no blocks in cells the registry calls empty; built features have ownership files and blocks still present; registered features have specs; OSM buildings no registered feature covers (warnings that block DONE until resolved or dismissed with a reason); leftover old-system files (STAGES, QUEUE, CURRENT-CELL, sign-offs). Hook verify into scripts/run_tests.py / dryrun_reset where sensible. tasks.title: Bug: real ground drops ghost-ground ownership across the whole cell, so undo restores air instead of the substrate (cause of #123 pit)
tasks.notes: ROOT CAUSE of #123 (found 2026-10-26 from journal + blobs only, read-only, world southampton-build). Undo restore values come from cell_journal._prepare_undo (lib/journal/cell_journal.py ~1168): erase[p] = under-owner state (ownership with the target seqs skipped) else AIR. Ownership comes from _cell_owners (~812), which at line ~831 deletes EVERY ghost-ground owner in a cell as soon as a real 'ground' build lands there ('real ground supersedes ghost ground'). That assumes the real ground apply physically overwrote all ghost blocks, but a ground plan writes only its own positions (highfield_48_m44_ground seq 104/110: n=7586 for the whole cell, surface only, nothing under features). The ghost substrate below (stone y1-52, top concrete y53) is still in the world but no journal entry owns it, so undo falls back to air. JUBILEE NUMBERS: undo seq 114 (n=36756): in cell 48,-44, 10003 positions written as air where ghost_48_m44_ground (seq 68) has solid blocks. These are the pit: e.g. 6244,-5515 build 90 wrote stone y49-52 + smooth_stone y53 over ghost stone/black_concrete; undo wrote air y49-53, exactly the 5-block pit with vertical walls (the edge is the jubilee footprint). In cells 48,-43 / 49,-44 / 49,-43 (no real ground yet) undo correctly restored the ghost blocks (10878+713+1934 positions). Contract pinned by lib/journal/test_cell_journal.py:384 test_ghost_ground_then_real_ground_supersedes (line 392 asserts that a ghost block the ground plan never wrote is unowned), ADR 004 point 5 and docs/specs/cell-journal-interface.md:68. SECONDARY GAP (same fix area): with no owner anywhere, undo assumes air, so blocks in the world that no journal entry owns are lost. At x=6209 z -5513..-5505 before_jubilee has stone to y53 while ghost 68/12 top is y49 (light_gray/black concrete); undo will leave a 4-block step there even with the supersession fixed. Where those blocks came from is unknown (not any journalled plan in these cells). FIX: (1) supersession only where the real ground covers: per column the ground plan writes, drop ghost owners above that column's real top (and at its positions, already handled by later-wins); keep the ghost substrate below and every ghost column the ground plan does not cover (under features). Update test 384 and add a test: ghost ground, feature over it, real ground elsewhere in the cell, undo feature -> ghost blocks restored, no air. Check what reconcile and the ghost.ground view now report for the kept substrate (it must not be 'missing' or re-queue ghost ground). (2) journal the prior blocks at Build begin (read_many over the planned positions, stored as a second blob, e.g. 'prior'); undo uses the under-owner when it is a real owner, else the prior blob, else air (old entries without a prior blob keep today's rule). Benchmark the read on a ~60k-block feature. (3) ADR 004 / interface spec: record the narrower supersession and the prior-blob rule. DONE WHEN: a scratch-world build + real ground in the same cell + undo leaves the box identical to before_<plan> (structure diff, zero differences), with tests for both rules. If it works, #123 closes with it (its remaining steps are the readback-vs-snapshot check, the purge-skill step and the jubilee repair). Landed on main via ship_branch (task/124-ghost-ground-ownership, bfd95d8).

tasks.title: Bug: element undo digs into intact ground (pit after purging a feature); undo must restore the actual pre-build world
tasks.notes: FOUND purging jubilee_w93729745 (2026-10-26, world southampton-build, cells 48,-44 / 48,-43 / 49,-44 / 49,-43). Journal: build begin seq 90 (strict False, modifies [], blob 71b85862caf886865f515ea3110daf21, n=61627), undo begin seq 114 (strict True, targets [90], blob 7a1bf5423a5cc3fe4434c72a19b0f405, n=36756). Structures: southampton_refine:before_jubilee_w93729745 and before_undo_jubilee_w93729745_20261026225610, both box (6208,37,-5535)-(6279,67,-5472). SYMPTOM: a pit about 5 blocks deep, vertical walls, around x 6244 z -5508..-5525. Live top_y (first free block) there is 49, before-snapshot 54. z -5500 and -5530 match. 17 sampled columns, not a full diff. EVIDENCE (read-only): (a) the build did NOT dig: in before_jubilee and before_undo the ground below y=53 is identical (stone y44-52 at 6244,-5520 and 6244,-5515; only y53 differs, black_concrete vs smooth_stone floor). Only 43 positions were solid before but air at undo time. (b) The undo's blob writes different ground than the real pre-build world: for x=6209, z -5513..-5505 it writes air over y37-53 where before_jubilee has stone to 53; at z -5504 it writes stone to y48 then concrete at 49. So undo restored a stale ground model (surface about y49) instead of the world as it was before the build (surface about y53/54). Likely cause: the restore values come from the journal's ground-owner plan (ghost_48_m43_ground etc.), which disagrees with the real before state. Not confirmed; read lib/site/site_kit.py undo (line ~1064) and cell_journal first. WHY IT WAS MISSED: undo's clean readback passed (it checks against its own targets) and cell_registry reconcile showed only 62 ground findings (40 missing, 22 foreign), which --fix repaired. Neither compares with the before_<plan> structure. HOW TO COMPARE: structure_file_read returns base64 gzip NBT (too big for chat, it lands in a tool-results file); parse with lib/blocks/nbt_read.py read_named_root (lists are Tag.value=(kind, items); pos is relative to the box origin). block_get_top_y returns the first free y, so the top solid block is one lower. RegionBlocks (lib/blocks/region_blocks.py) reads the world read-only after a save. Blob format: zstd json {rle: [[x,z,y0,y1,state]]}. PLAN: (1) reproduce on a small feature in a scratch world: build, undo, diff the box against before_<plan>; (2) find where undo takes its restore values and make them the begin-time snapshot of the actual world, or journal the prior blocks at apply; (3) make undo readback compare the whole box with the before_<plan> structure and fail on any difference; (4) regression test in lib/site/test_element_undo.py; (5) purge skill step 3: compare the footprint with the snapshot, not only reconcile. JUBILEE REPAIR (separate, world work): restore_structure_backup.py jubilee_w93729745 dry run, then cell_registry reconcile; it bypasses the journal. CAUSE FOUND (2026-10-26): see #124. Not the ground-owner plan disagreeing with the world in general: in cell 48,-44 the real highfield ground (seq 104/110) made the fold drop all ghost-ground ownership in that cell, so undo had no earlier owner under jubilee and wrote air (10003 positions; the pit). A smaller unowned-block gap (x=6209 strip) is also covered by #124. #124 is the prerequisite; if its scratch-world undo diff is clean, close #123 alongside it after the jubilee repair and the purge-skill check. UNBLOCKED after #124: ownership + prior-blob fix landed. Remaining for #123: undo readback-vs-before_<plan> structure check; purge skill footprint-vs-snapshot step; jubilee world repair (restore_structure_backup + reconcile) — world work. DONE 2026-10-26: undo begin compares erase plan to before_<plan> structure and abandons on drift (verify_erase_matches_before); structure_nbt reader; element_undo regression tests; purge §3 footprint-vs-snapshot. Jubilee pit repaired live (1712 stone fills where substrate was air; structure_load failed on size — fill path). Merge via ship_branch.

Raised 2026-10-28 from the SUSU entrance covered-area issue (I-021, snag S-027; also the covered-entrance part of I-018). Cause class: Capability. facade_plan entrances accept and validate awning_like (lib/builds/facade_plan.py) but plan_doors in lib/builds/feature_build.py never reads it; awning_like is only built from free-standing details rows. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py, colocated tests in lib/builds/test_feature_build.py (one per kind, none builds nothing, depth changes extent, unresolved entrance builds no cover, existing details awning_like row unchanged), rules/feature-builds.md (geometry per kind, plan_doors reads it). The spec edit that adds awning_like to the SUSU entrance (susu_w33830305) is part of the check, not the code change: the designer or rebuild adds it after reading the photo. Check S-027: after rebuilding susu_w33830305 with an awning_like entry on its entrance, a roof stands over the door in game and the door is still walkable.
